detail.description: The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Sacramento District (SPK), anticipates solicitation of a requirement for design-build (DB) and design-bid-build (DBB) – Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) for Construction Services in support of SPK’s Military Boundary and Area of Responsibility. Specific needs will be determined based upon project requirements as described in each task order. Selected firms will work on a variety of projects that may include but not necessarily limited to new construction (including new work, additions, alterations, maintenance, and repairs) of commercial and institutional buildings and related structures. Anticipated work may include the following: new construction, additions, alterations, renovations, repairs, and maintenance of facilities and supporting infrastructure. detail.title: REPAIR LIVE FIRE TRAINING FACILITY AIRCRAFT MOCK-UP
detail.description: The 910th Airlift Wing requires repair and corrective work to the Aircraft Fire Training Facility (AFTF) aircraft mock-up located at Youngstown Air Reserve Station. An inspection and evaluation of the Aircraft Fire Training Facility was conducted in August 2025 and finalized in April 2026. The assessment identified deficiencies affecting the facility's burner and ignition systems, structural components, corrosion protection, sprinkler system, propane distribution and emergency shutoff systems, control systems, and associated components. The contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, tools, transportation, testing, quality control, and other items and services necessary to complete the work identified in the Statement of Work, drawings, specifications, and solicitation attachments. Troubleshooting, repair, and/or replacement of the Tail Engine Burner, Wheel Well Burner, Flight Deck Burner, and Cargo Area Burner and associated ignition systems. Repair or replacement of burner ignition components as required to restore proper operation. Replacement of the malfunctioning cargo-area sprinkler head and restoration of proper drainage functionality. Structural steel repairs and corrosion remediation beneath portions of the aircraft mock-up. Corrosion repair beneath flight-deck stairs and around door assemblies. Repair and/or replacement of the warped R2 door and warped grating near the cargo-fire area. Certified welding and associated aircraft mock-up repairs. Installation/restoration of an emergency energy shutoff capability at the propane storage area. Installation of required solenoid valve(s) in the LPG/propane distribution system. Correction of deficiencies involving legacy pneumatic shutoff valves. Required control-system repairs/upgrades. Associated maintenance, testing, and corrective actions necessary to provide a complete and functional system. Applicable standards identified in the Government's technical documentation include, as applicable: USAF Technical Order 35E1-2-13-1 NFPA 54 NFPA 58 NFPA 70 NFPA 1003 NFPA 1402

detail.title: HSCG82-26-1-0047 Office Space/Lease McAllen TX
detail.description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) currently seeks to lease office and administrative support space in McAllen, Texas, meeting the operational requirements outlined below. The USCG is looking for existing, modern, and move-in-ready commercial configurations to minimize initial federal buildout and conversion expenses. The building must be located within a professional office environment, corporate park, or commercial business district with a professional appearance, suitable for a military branch command headquarters. Summary of Key Lease Requirements: State: Texas City: McAllen Delineated Area: Directly off or with immediate access to Highway 2, between Exits 69E and 69C. Minimum Space (ABOA SF): approx. 6,500 ANSI/BOMA Office Area Square Feet Maximum Space (ABOA SF): approx. 8,500 ANSI/BOMA Office Area Square Feet Rentable Space (RSF): approx. Minimum 7,500 Rentable Square Feet Space Type: Fully serviced commercial office space (Class A or Class B). Lease Term: One (1) Year Firm Term with five (5) optional one-year renewal options, exercised at the sole discretion of the Government. Occupancy Date: Target occupancy is immediate upon lease award and completion of any necessary tenant improvements. Lease Type: Fully Serviced (Full Service). Quoted rates must include all utilities, heating, ventilation, air conditioning (HVAC), janitorial services, trash removal, and building maintenance. SPECIFIC SPACE & TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS Offered properties must currently accommodate or be capable of being modified to meet the following physical and technical requirements: Dedicated Support & Conference Areas Coast Guard Administrative Coordination Office: A designated administrative work area capable of housing standard workstations and secure command filing storage. Coast Guard Support & Medical Readiness Room: A partitioned space configured for administrative support and staff readiness personnel. This area must feature a sink with hot and cold potable water, storage cabinets, and cleanable surfaces. Command Conference Room: A professional meeting space configured to comfortably accommodate 12–15 personnel, featuring structural capability for audio-visual, briefings, and teleconferencing equipment. Dedicated USCG Telecom/Server Room: A secure, climate-controlled room specifically designated to house Coast Guard IT networking equipment, servers, and communication infrastructure. The room must feature dedicated, independent cooling operating continuously (24/7/365), space for a standard 4-post server rack, and secure access control. Common Areas & Facilities Break Room Area: A designated break room or space adjacent to the main administrative area containing a full-sized refrigerator with active water line hookups. Communications & Roof Rights Antenna and Satellite Roof Access: The Lessor shall grant the USCG non-exclusive roof access for the installation, maintenance, and operation of critical communications equipment (including VHF/UHF tactical radio antennas, GPS receivers, and satellite dishes) required for regional coordination. Dedicated Cable Conduits: The Lessor must provide secure, weather-tight conduit runs (minimum 2-inch diameter) leading directly from the roof-mounted equipment area to the dedicated USCG Telecom/Server Room to facilitate secure cabling. Utilities, Power, & Access Backup Power System: The building must have access to a commercial generator (or robust battery backup system if utilizing solar power) configured to automatically transfer and supply uninterrupted power to the Telecom/Server Room, primary coordination spaces, emergency lighting, and building access systems during municipal power outages. Potable Water System: The property must have a reliable potable water system. If the property relies on a water cistern, the Lessor must install and maintain a certified filtration and sterilization system. detail.pointOfContact: Ai Gillard - Contracting Officer <ai.gillard.ln@us.navy.mil>; Samantha Salgado <samantha.c.salgado.civ@us.navy.mil>
detail.description: Naval Supply Systems Command (NAVSUP) Fleet Logistics Center Yokosuka (FLCY), on behalf of the U.S. Naval Ship Repair Facility and Japan Regional Maintenance Center (SRF-JRMC), is conducting market research to identify interested and capable contractors with ship repair, modernization, and dry-docking maintenance execution experience. The Government anticipates requiring support for projected dry-docking Selected Restricted Availabilities (DSRA), Selected Restricted Availabilities (SRA), CMAV (Continuous Maintenance Availability), SIA (Surface Incremental Availability), and other maintenance availabilities for forward-deployed naval forces (FDNF). Work will be performed aboard vessels located at Commander, Fleet Activities Yokosuka (CFAY), Yokosuka, Japan. The anticipated scope of work encompasses the following trade categories and technical disciplines: <Anticipated Trade Categories > Miscellaneous Hull Structure (foundations, stacks, sea chests, decks) Miscellaneous Propulsion Plant Systems (main engines, shafting, reduction gear, lube oil purifiers) Miscellaneous Electric Plant Generators (switchboards, lighting distribution) Miscellaneous Command/Surveillance Systems (navigation, communications, radar, sonar) Miscellaneous Auxiliary Systems (air conditioning, heating, fresh water, ballast, damage control)​ Miscellaneous Outfit/Furnishings (floor plates & grating, ladders, living spaces, work shops) Miscellaneous Armament (guns, mounts, small arms, munitions storage, ammo handling) Integrated Engineering (ILS engineering, planning production, program management) This Sources Sought Notice should not be construed as a formal solicitation or an obligation on the part of the U.S. Government. Any information provided to the U.S. Government is strictly voluntary and at no cost to the U.S. Government. The purpose of this notice is to determine interested parties, availability, capabilities, and qualifications. The U.S. Government intends to use responses to the sources sought notice to make an appropriate acquisition decision for the following requirement(s): Contract Type: Single award Firm-Fixed-Price Service Contract Prospective contractors must possess a Master Ship Repair Agreement (MSRA) or Agreement for Boat Repair (ABR) with NAVSUP FLCY at the time of contract award to meet the requirements of DFARS 217.71 Master Agreement for Repair and Alteration of Vessels (MARAV). It is the responsibility of the Contractor to establish and acquire all necessary licenses, regulatory compliance, approvals and permits prior to commencing shipbuilding or ship repair related businesses specific to Japan. Contractors doing business in Japan are subject to all applicable Japanese laws, including the Shipbuilding Act (Act No. 129 of 1950), the Small Shipbuilding Industry Law (Law No. 119 of 1966), and all environmental laws (e.g., The Water Pollution Prevention Act (No. 138 of 1970). Please refer to the following posting in SAM.gov. detail.title: Design-Build Repair and Renovation of the Gulf Marine Service Facility (GMSF) & Wharf Repairs, in Pascagoula, Mississippi
detail.description: Project Title: Design-Build Repair and Renovation of the Gulf Marine Service Facility (GMSF) & Wharf Repairs, in Pascagoula, Mississippi Location: 151 Watts Ave, Pascagoula, MS 39567 Classification and General Information: This requirement will be issued as a Total Small Business Set-Aside. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code associated with this procurement is 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The Small Business Administration standard of $45.0 million dollars in annual receipts averaged over a business’s latest three (3) complete fiscal years or (except in the Business Loan, Disaster Loan Programs, Surety Bond Guarantee, and SBIC Programs) five (5) complete fiscal years to determine the average annual receipts. If a business hasn’t been in business for five (5) years, multiply its average weekly revenue by 52 to determine its average annual receipts. This requirement will be a Total Small Business Set-Aside, and the contractor shall be selected using Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) Part 36.101-2 Use of Two-Phase Design-Build Selection Procedures and RFO Part 15.1 Presolicitation and Solicitation procedures. This procurement will be competitive, utilizing the Highest-Technically Rated with a Fair and Reasonable Process approach based on the solicitations’s stated budgetary constraints (affordability) under the Best Value (RFO Part 15.103). The approach prioritizes the best possible performance, provided the price is determined to be fair and reasonable and within the guidelines of the Government’s stated budget. During each phase, all proposals are initially evaluated based solely on the non-price factors specified in the solicitation. Only the price of the highest-ranked technical proposal is then evaluated to ensure it is fair, reasonable and does not exceed our stated budget. All evaluation factors other than cost or price, when combined, are significantly more important than cost or price. This requirement will result in a Firm-Fixed-Price contract for design and construction services. Background Overview: The GMSF is a critical NOAA asset located in Pascagoula, Mississippi, and is a shared-use site for both the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) and the Office of Marine and Aviation Operations (OMAO). The facility consists of a berthing wharf and pier, seawall, and upland warehouse buildings essential for supporting NOAA's mission in the Gulf of America Region. See Figure 1 for the GMSF site plan (See Attachment). The facility has sustained damage from recent hurricane and storm events, primarily affecting the wharf structure. Additionally, the steel sheet pile wall has sustained damage from exposure to the Pascagoula River, resulting in section loss of the sheets and subsequent loss of fill material behind the seawall. This loss of material has resulted in sink holes in the wharf operational area. The existing wharf and pier is approximately 540 feet long and 26 feet wide, and was constructed in three sections (referred to as the North, Middle and South sections). The wharf structure is integral with a steel sheet pile seawall. Each wharf section has been repaired in some form over the past several decades, primarily to address the failing seawall. A portion of the wharf overhangs the Pascagoula River. See Figure 2 for a typical section through the wharf (See Attachment). As-built drawings for each section of wharf are available and will be provided with the formally issued solicitation documents. NOAA’s ships homeported at GMSF are operated by two separate line offices - NMFS and OMAO. Mooring configurations at GMSF vary based on the operations of each line office. Refer to Table 1 (See Attachment) for information regarding the size of the NOAA ships homeported at GMSF, and to Figure 3 (See Attachment) for example mooring arrangements. detail.title: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement
detail.pointOfContact: Connie L. Ferguson <Connie.L.Ferguson@usace.army.mil>; Levi R. Speth <Levi.R.Speth@usace.army.mil>
detail.description: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement. USACE, Pittsburgh District, has an upcoming requirement to replace the siding of the Resource Managers Office at Youghiogheny River Lake. The work described herein shall be performed at the Youghiogheny Resource Managers Office (RMO) building located within the Youghiogheny River Lake project area in Confluence, Pennsylvania. The building currently serves as administrative office space for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The RMO building was constructed in 1986 and is a multi-level, timber-framed structure built into the hillside overlooking the impoundment side of the dam. The exterior walls consist of 2x6 wood stud framing with 6-inch fiberglass batt insulation (R-19, foil-faced). Interior partitions consist of 2x4 wood studs with 1/2-inch gypsum wallboard. The existing exterior wall assembly consists of 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing with 5/8-inch cedar-faced T1-11 plywood siding, for a combined nominal thickness of 1-1/8 inches. Exterior trim and fascia consist of various widths of cedar lumber. The building is supported by cast-in-place concrete footings and 12-inch concrete masonry unit (CMU) foundation walls. The rear wall section and balcony framing are supported by 4 feet-0 inches wide by 5 feet-0 inches deep concrete footings, laminated wood columns (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches), and laminated wood beams (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches).This project consists of the removal and replacement of the existing exterior wall cladding system. The Contractor shall remove and dispose of the existing T1-11 siding and 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing in their entirety. The Contractor shall furnish and install a new exterior wall assembly consisting of 1/2-inch APA-rated structural wood sheathing, a continuous weather-resistive barrier (WRB), 3/8-inch nominal preservative-treated wood furring strips, and 5/16-inch fiber cement lap siding in accordance with manufacturer requirements. The new wall assembly is intended to match the existing wall thickness (approximately 1-1/8 inches) to maintain alignment with existing window and door openings. Minor dimensional variation within normal construction tolerances are acceptable and shall not require modification or resetting of existing windows and doors. The Contractor shall not reset, relocate, or otherwise modify existing windows and doors. Furring strips shall be installed vertically over the WRB at a maximum spacing of 16 inches on center and shall be fastened through the sheathing into wall framing members. Fiber cement siding shall be installed horizontally over the furring strips and fastened through the furring and sheathing into wall framing members. Furring strips are intended to provide a drainage and ventilation cavity and shall not be used as the sole fastening substrate for the fiber cement lap siding. The Contractor shall ensure that all fiber cement lap siding edges are supported by framing members or approved blocking in accordance with manufacturer requirements. The Contractor shall furnish and install all required trim at windows, doors, corners, and transitions. Trim material shall be fiber cement. The cedar hand railing on the balconys is to be new capped PVC or capped composite decking of matching color to fiber cement board siding. The Contractor shall provide complete flashing at all required locations, including but not limited to head flashing at windows and doors, Z-flashing at horizontal joints and transitions, and kick-out flashing at roof-to-wall intersections. All flashing shall be integrated with the WRB in a shingle-lap manner to maintain a continuous drainage plane. The work shall be completed within 180 after written Notice to Proceed. Disclosure of Magnitude of Construction (FAR 36.204 and DFARS 236.204) The acquisition will be procured as 100% Set-Aside for Small Business. detail.description: Request for Quote (RFQ): Water Tanker/Pump Repair FA930126Q0030 This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number FA930126Q00301 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ) for Fire Truck Water Tanker/Pumper Repair. This acquisition is set aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. Background: The 412 Logistics Readiness Squadron Vehicle Management Flight needs contracted vendor services to replace the agent water tank assembly and associated components on Fire Department Water Tender with registration number 11L00144, which was delivered to Vehicle Management with multiple leaks on top of the tank and a noticeable sag in the center when fully loaded, causing the tank to rub the body and damage the exterior integrity of the tank. Upon inspection, it was found that the damage was a result of the structural integrity of the agent tank that had diminished over the years. It is beyond the capabilities of the vehicle management flight technicians to repair. See attached SOW for further information and included photos of the vehicle for reference. Product service code (PSC) J042 and North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) 811310 are being considered for this requirement. Basis for Award : Comparative Evaluation The Government intends to award a contract to the responsible offeror whose quotation, conforming to the solicitation, is determined to represent the best value to the Government. Evaluation Methodology In accordance with RFO 12.203, the Government will utilize a Comparative Evaluation process. Rather than rating or scoring each quotation individually against a rigid, predetermined evaluation rubric, the Government will compare all received quotations directly against one another to identify which submission offers the most advantageous solution. Evaluation Factors for Comparison The Government will compare quotations based on the following factors to determine which provides the best overall value: Evaluation Factors: *Technical Capability - the Government will compare the proposed features, methods, and technical solutions of each quotation directly against the others. The goal is to determine which proposed approach provides the greatest benefit, utility, and likelihood of successfully meeting or exceeding the requirements outlined in the Statement of Work (SOW). *Past Performance - the Government will compare the recent and relevant past performance records of the competing offerors. The Government may utilize the Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS) and other independent government or commercial sources to determine which offeror presents the lowest performance risk and the highest probability of success. *Price -the Government will compare the proposed prices to ensure they are fair and reasonable. Price will be evaluated in conjunction with the non-price factors to determine if the relative benefits of a specific quotation justify its proposed cost. *Delivery and warranty Selection Decision: Because this is a comparative evaluation, the Government is not required to establish a predefined rating scale. The Government reserves the right to select a quotation that is not the lowest priced if the direct comparison reveals that the technical superiority or stronger past performance of a higher-priced quotation provides a better overall value to the Government. The final decision will be based on a documented rationale explaining why the successful quotation is the best value for the Government.
